title: Restoring Gold Standard Science
aiSummary: This Executive Order directs federal agencies to adopt rigorous “Gold Standard Science” practices to restore public trust in the integrity of federally funded scientific research. Citing past misuse of scientific data, reproducibility concerns, and politicization of science, the order requires that scientific information used in policy decisions be transparent, reproducible, and objectively evaluated. Within 30 days, the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) must issue guidance outlining these standards, after which agencies must update their scientific integrity policies and report implementation actions within 60 days. Agencies are required to disclose influential data and models (with limited exceptions), communicate uncertainty and assumptions clearly, and apply a “weight of scientific evidence” approach in decision-making. Interim policies revert to those in place as of January 19, 2021, and actions taken between January 20, 2021, and January 20, 2025, must be reviewed for compliance. Each agency must also establish internal processes to address violations. The order applies to all employees and contractors involved in scientific activities, with limited waivers permitted by OMB and OSTP.
deliverable:
OSTP must issue guidance on “Gold Standard Science” within 30 days.

Agencies must update scientific integrity policies promptly after OSTP guidance.

Agencies must report to OSTP on implementation within 60 days of OSTP guidance.

Agencies and employees must follow new scientific data rules within 30 days.

Agencies must make influential scientific data and models public as practicable.

Agencies must review and revise policies issued between Jan. 20, 2021–Jan. 20, 2025.

Agencies must revoke changes made under the Jan. 27, 2021 Presidential Memorandum.

Agencies must review actions from Jan. 20, 2021–Jan. 20, 2025 for compliance with the EO.

Agencies must establish internal processes to evaluate scientific integrity violations.

Agencies must include scientific integrity standards in contractor terms where practicable.

Agency heads may request waivers from OMB and OSTP on a case-by-case basis.

title: Delivering Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing to American Patients
aiSummary: This Executive Order seeks to align U.S. prescription drug prices with those in comparably developed countries by implementing a “most-favored-nation” pricing strategy. It directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to communicate price targets to pharmaceutical manufacturers within 30 days and to facilitate direct-to-consumer programs offering drugs at the most-favored-nation price. If significant progress is not made, the order authorizes additional actions, including proposed rulemaking, importation certifications, antitrust enforcement, export controls, and potential FDA regulatory reviews. The order also calls on the Department of Commerce and USTR to address international pricing practices that contribute to disproportionately high drug costs for American consumers.
deliverable: Communicate most-favored-nation price targets to pharmaceutical manufacturers — within 30 days

title: Regulatory Relief to Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines
aiSummary: This Executive Order aims to strengthen the U.S. pharmaceutical supply chain by removing regulatory barriers to domestic manufacturing. It directs the FDA, EPA, and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to review and streamline applicable regulations and guidance within 180 days to improve the timeliness and predictability of agency review processes. The order also calls for enhanced inspections of foreign pharmaceutical facilities, increased transparency on inspection activities, and centralized coordination of environmental permits for new manufacturing sites. The policy goal is to create a more resilient, competitive, and secure domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing base.

Improve risk-based inspection regime for overseas manufacturing facilities; increase transparency on inspection frequency by country/manufacturer. - 90 days.

EPA as lead agency under NEPA for pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities requiring Environmental Impact Statements; designate a single point of contact for applicants. – Immediate.

title: Improving the Safety and Security of Biological Research
aiSummary: This EO directs enhanced oversight and restrictions on U.S. federally funded gain-of-function research, particularly involving foreign entities and countries of concern. It halts funding for certain high-risk life sciences research lacking sufficient biosafety oversight and mandates the development of revised federal policies for such research within 120 days. The order also requires improved enforcement mechanisms, expanded transparency measures, and a strategy to address risks associated with non-federally funded research. Key agencies are tasked with updating biosafety frameworks and implementing strict conditions in grant agreements to ensure compliance.
deliverable:
Immediate halt to federal funding of dangerous gain-of-function research in countries of concern – Effective immediately (Sec. 3(a)).

Suspension of federally funded dangerous research pending updated policy – Effective immediately (Sec. 3(b)).

Revise or replace dual-use/gain-of-function oversight policy – Within 120 days (Sec. 4(a)).

Revise or replace the Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening – Within 90 days (Sec. 4(b)).

Develop strategy to govern non-federally funded dangerous research – Within 180 days (Sec. 5).

Submit legislative proposal to fill gaps in authority for regulating such research – Within 180 days (Sec. 5).

Establish public reporting mechanism for federally and non-federally funded dangerous research – Timeline not specified, but tied to updated policy under Sec. 4(a) (Sec. 6).

Include enforcement terms in all future life-science research grants/contracts – Effective upon implementation of the order (Sec. 7).

title: Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First
aiSummary: This EO seeks to optimize Federal health care programs, intellectual property protections, and safety regulations to provide access to prescription drugs at lower costs. The EO directs various agency actions to achieve this goal.
deliverable: Propose and seek comment on guidance for the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program for initial price applicability year 2028 and manufacturer effectuation of maximum fair price under such program in 2026, 2027, and 2028 (60 days); Recommendations to stabilize and reduce Medicare Part D premiums (180 days); HHS Secretary to develop and implement a rulemaking plan and select for testing a payment model to improve the ability of the Medicare program (1 year); Secretary shall publish in Federal Register a plan to conduct a survey to determine the hospital acquisition costs for outpatient drugs (180 days); Recommendations to President regarding how to best ensure that manufacturers pay accurate Medicaid drug rebates, promote payment innovation, link payments for drugs to the value, and support state drug spending management (180 days); Secretary shall take action to ensure future grants (under 330(e) of the Public Health Service Act, as amended, 42 U.S.C. 254b(e)) are conditioned upon establishing practices to make insulin and injectable epinephrine available at discounted prices for those with qualifying low incomes (90 days); Provide recommendations to President to promote a competitive, efficient, resilient, and transparent pharmaceutical value chain (90 days); Secretary shall report recommendations to accelerate the approval of generics and biosimilars and improve OTC drug reclassification (180 days); Secretary shall take steps to streamline the Importation Program under section 804 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (90 days); Propose regulations to prevent shifts to more expensive drug administration settings (180 days); Secretary shall evaluate and propose regulations to improve employer health plan fiduciary transparency and indirect pharmacy benefit manager compensation (180 days); Secretary shall conduct join public listening sessions and issue report a with recommendations to reduce anti-competitive practices by pharmaceutical manufacturers (180 days).

title: Making America Healthy Again by Empowering Patients with Clear, Accurate, and Actionable Healthcare Pricing Information
aiSummary: This EO states that the Federal Government will promote universal access to clear and accurate healthcare prices. The Secretaries of the Treasury, Labor, and HHS are directed to take all necessary and appropriate action to rapidly implement and enforce the healthcare price transparency regulations issued pursuant to Executive Order 13877 (June 24, 2019, Improving Price and Quality Transparency in American Healthcare to Put Patients First) to require the disclosure of the actual prices of items and services, not estimates, issue updated guidance or proposed regulatory action ensuring pricing information is standardized and easily comparable across hospitals and health plans, and issue guidance or proposed regulatory action updating enforcement policies designed to ensure compliance with the transparent reporting of complete, accurate, and meaningful data within 90 days.

title: Establishing the President's Make America Healthy Again Commission

Further, the Make America Healthy Again Commission is established with the initial mission to advise the President how to address childhood chronic disease (reports due in 100 days and 180 days).

title: Enforcing the Hyde Amendment

title: Aligning United States Core Childhood Vaccine Recommendations with Best Practices from Peer, Developed Countries
aiSummary: This memorandum directs federal health officials to review childhood vaccine recommendations from peer, developed countries and update U.S. guidelines if superior, evidence-based practices are identified, while maintaining access to all currently available vaccines.

title: Increasing Medical Marijuana and Cannabidiol Research
aiSummary: This EO directs the expedited rescheduling of marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III, acknowledging its accepted medical use and reduced abuse potential. It further calls for a regulatory framework and improved research on both medical marijuana and hemp-derived CBD products, including clear guidance on THC limits and accurate product labeling. The order aims to close gaps in medical knowledge so patients and providers may access safe, effective, and well-informed treatment options.

title: Prosecuting Burning of the American Flag
aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to prioritize enforcement of laws against acts of American Flag desecration that incite violence or violate existing content-neutral statutes, consistent with First Amendment limits. It also authorizes immigration-related penalties for foreign nationals involved in flag desecration and encourages federal coordination with state and local authorities for further action.

title: Measures to End Cashless Bail and Enforce the Law in the District of Columbia
aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to take all lawful steps to halt cashless bail policies in Washington, D.C., prioritizing the pretrial detention of criminal suspects who pose a threat to public safety and encouraging federally-supported charges and custody whenever possible. Additionally, it instructs the Attorney General and executive departments to review existing police and judicial practices, and to use available administrative and budgetary actions to press D.C. to restore cash bail for offenders considered dangerous.

title: Taking Steps to End Cashless Bail to Protect Americans
aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to identify and potentially suspend or terminate federal funding to states and local jurisdictions that have substantially eliminated cash bail for defendants charged with serious crimes. It establishes a policy that federal resources should not support jurisdictions with cashless bail practices, in order to promote public safety and ensure pretrial detention of individuals who pose a risk to society.
deliverable: AG shall submit a list of states and local jurisdictions that have substantially eliminated cash bail as a potential condition of pretrial release from custody of crimes that pose a clear threat to public safety and order (30 days).

title: Executive Grant of Clemency for Devon Archer

title: Preventing Abuses of the Legal System and the Federal Court
aiSummary: This Memo directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of DHS to prioritize enforcement of their respective regulations governing attorney conduct and discipline.  See, e.g., 8 C.F.R. 292.1 et seq.; 8 C.F.R. 1003.101 et seq.; 8 C.F.R. 1292.19. The AG shall take all appropriate action to refer for disciplinary action any attorney whose conduct in Federal court or before any component of the Federal Government appears to violate professional conduct rules. When the AG determines that conduct by an attorney or law firm in litigation against the Federal Government warrants seeking sanctions or other disciplinary action, the Attorney General shall recommend to the President any additional steps that may be taken, including reassessment of security clearances or termination of any Federal contract for which the relevant attorney or law firm has been hired. The AG shall review conduct by attorneys or their law firms in litigation against the Federal Government over the last 8 years and any misconduct that may warrant additional action shall be recommended to the President. AG shall periodically update the president on progress.

title: Ensuring the Enforcement of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 65(c)
aiSummary: This proclamation states that it is the policy of the United States to demand that parties seeking injunctions against the Federal Government must cover the costs and damages incurred if the Government is ultimately found to have been wrongfully enjoined or restrained and that “Federal courts should hold litigants accountable for their misrepresentations and ill-granted injunctions.” The heads of agencies shall, in consultation with the Attorney General, ensure that their respective agencies properly request under Rule 65(c) that Federal district courts require plaintiffs to post security equal to the Federal Government’s potential costs and damages from a wrongly issued injunction. The scope of this directive covers all lawsuits filed against the Federal Government seeking an injunction where agencies can show expected monetary damages or costs from the requested preliminary relief, unless extraordinary circumstances justify an exception.

title: Additional Measures to Address the Crime Emergency in the District of Columbia
aiSummary: This EO directs multiple federal agencies to take immediate measures to address public safety and disorder in the District of Columbia, including hiring additional law enforcement personnel, forming specialized units, and increasing oversight of housing and transit conditions. title: Declaring a Crime Emergency in the District of Columbia
aiSummary: This EO declares a public safety emergency in the District of Columbia due to rising violent crime and directs the Mayor to provide the services of the Metropolitan Police Department for federal purposes, with operational control delegated to the Attorney General. The Attorney General is tasked with monitoring the situation, consulting with appropriate officials, and regularly updating the President.

title: Restoring the Death Penalty and Protecting Public Safety
aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of the US to ensure laws authorizing capital punishment are respected and implemented. The Attorney General shall pursue the death penalty "for all crimes of a severity demanding its use" including every federal capital crime involving (1) the murder of a law-enforcement officer or (2) a capital crime committed by an alien illegally present in this country. The Attorney General shall also encourage the same for state capital charges, including ensuring that states have sufficient supplies of lethal injection drugs. The EO also directs various other actions to encourage capital punishment, including: modifying the Justice Manual; evaluating the cases of the 37 individuals who received federal death sentence commutations from President Biden, including encouraging evaluation of state charges; seeking overruling of Supreme Court precedents that hinder capital punishment; and prioritizing public safety and prosecution of violent crime.

title: Department of War Security for the Protection of Federal Personnel and Property in Illinois

title: Enforcing the Death Penalty Laws in the District of Columbia to Deter and Punish the Most Heinous Crimes
aiSummary: The President has directed federal prosecutors to fully enforce the death penalty in the District of Columbia, making it a priority for crimes warranting capital punishment, especially in light of recent public safety concerns in the nation's capital. The memorandum instructs the Attorney General and the U.S. Attorney for D.C. to seek the death penalty in all appropriate cases, ensuring robust implementation of federal capital punishment laws.

title: Countering Domestic Terrorism and Organized Political Violence
aiSummary: The President has directed federal agencies to implement a comprehensive strategy to disrupt and dismantle organized domestic terrorist networks responsible for political violence, including targeted intimidation, doxing, and attacks on federal officers and facilities. This strategy includes increased investigation, prosecution, financial tracking, and potential designation of domestic terrorist organizations, making the prevention of politically motivated terrorism a national law enforcement priority.

title: Restoring Law and Order in Memphis
aiSummary: The President has established a Memphis Safe Task Force composed of federal, state, and local agencies to combat the city's high rates of violent crime through coordinated law enforcement, aggressive prosecution, and increased presence in affected neighborhoods. Additionally, the President has authorized the mobilization of Tennessee National Guard units to support public safety and Task Force operations, with ongoing assessment of whether further executive action is needed to restore law and order in Memphis.

title: Addressing Risks from Susman Godfrey
aiSummary: This EO directs a suspension pending review for any active security clearances held by individuals at Susman and a cessation of any government materials provided. Government contracting agencies shall, to the extent permissible by law, require Government contractors to disclose any business they do with Susman and whether that business is related to the subject of the Government contract. The heads of all agencies shall review all contracts with Susman or with entities that disclose doing business with it under subsection and take steps to terminate any contracts. The heads of all agencies shall provide guidance limiting official access from Federal Government buildings to employees of Susman when such access would threaten the national security of or otherwise be inconsistent with the interests of the United States and guidance limiting Government employees acting in their official capacity from engaging with Susman employees. Lastly, agency officials shall refrain from hiring employees of Susman, absent a waiver from the head of the agency, made in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.
deliverable: All agencies shall submit to the Director of OMB an assessment of contracts with Susman or with entities that do business with it effective as of the date of this order and any actions taken with respect to those contracts in accordance with this order (30 days).

title: Ending Crime and Disorder on America's Streets
agenciesImpacted: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
aiSummary: This Executive Order establishes a new federal policy approach toward homelessness, emphasizing public safety and the use of civil commitment and institutional treatment for individuals with serious mental illness or substance use disorders. It directs federal agencies to reassess grant priorities, discourage harm-reduction models, and enforce stricter standards for program participation and accountability. The order also aims to redirect funding toward programs that reduce homelessness and crime, while enhancing data-sharing with law enforcement and expanding requirements for housing programs.
deliverable:
Immediately: DOJ, HHS, HUD, and DOT must assess their discretionary grant programs to prioritize applicants meeting public safety and enforcement criteria.

Immediately: DOJ must ensure individuals arrested for federal crimes are evaluated under 18 U.S.C. § 4248 for civil commitment as sexually dangerous persons.

Immediately: DOJ must assess and deploy Emergency Federal Law Enforcement Assistance funds to support encampment removals.

Immediately: DOJ must assess whether federal resources can prevent the release of mentally ill detainees due to insufficient forensic bed capacity.

Immediately: DOJ must enhance in-custody housing release plan requirements at DOJ-run or funded facilities.

As appropriate: DOJ must seek reversal of precedents and termination of consent decrees that limit civil commitment efforts.

As appropriate: DOJ and HHS must assist states and municipalities with technical guidance and support for civil commitment and treatment programs.

As appropriate: HHS must redirect SAMHSA grants to exclude harm-reduction and safe consumption models.

As appropriate: HHS must provide technical assistance to outpatient treatment programs tied to civil commitment.

As appropriate: HHS must ensure funding for Federally Qualified Health Centers and Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics reduces homelessness.

As appropriate: DOJ must prioritize funding for drug courts and mental health courts.

As appropriate: HHS and HUD must raise performance standards and competitiveness among homelessness and transitional housing grant recipients.

As appropriate: HUD must require treatment participation as a condition of receiving housing assistance.

As appropriate: DOJ must review legality of grantees operating safe consumption sites and bring enforcement actions.

As appropriate: HUD must freeze assistance to recipients violating program terms related to illegal drug use.

As appropriate: HUD must revise regulations to permit women-and-children-only housing and exclude sex offenders from being housed with unrelated children.

As appropriate: HUD, in consultation with DOJ and HHS, must permit or require grantees to collect and share health data with law enforcement and public health entities.

title: Saving College Sports
agenciesImpacted: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
White House Office of Public Liaison
aiSummary: This Executive Order aims to stabilize and preserve college athletics in the United States by protecting non-revenue and women’s sports, prohibiting third-party pay-for-play arrangements, and clarifying the legal status of student-athletes. It directs federal agencies to use regulatory, funding, enforcement, and litigation tools to ensure fair treatment of athletes and preserve the educational and developmental benefits of collegiate sports. The order also calls for safeguards to ensure the continued contribution of college sports to the development of Olympic athletes.
deliverable:
Within 30 days: Secretary of Education, in consultation with DOJ, HHS, and FTC, must develop a plan to implement policies protecting non-revenue sports and prohibiting pay-for-play payments.

Immediately and ongoing: College athletic departments with revenue over $125 million must increase non-revenue sport scholarships and roster spots for the 2025–2026 season and beyond.

Immediately and ongoing: College athletic departments with revenue over $50 million must maintain non-revenue sport scholarships and roster spots for the 2025–2026 season and beyond.

Immediately and ongoing: College athletic departments with $50 million or less in revenue or no revenue sports must not disproportionately reduce non-revenue sport opportunities.

Immediately and ongoing: Any revenue-sharing plans must preserve or expand scholarships in non-revenue and women’s sports.

Immediately and ongoing: Universities must prohibit third-party pay-for-play arrangements, except fair-market NIL endorsements.

Immediately and ongoing: Secretary of Labor and NLRB must take steps to clarify the legal status of student-athletes to protect their educational opportunities.

Within 60 days: Attorney General and FTC Chairman must review and, if necessary, revise litigation positions and policies to preserve scholarships and protect against unreasonable legal challenges.

Within 60 days: Attorney General and FTC Chairman must develop a forward-looking plan for legal and regulatory protection of college athletics.

Ongoing: Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and Director of the White House Office of Public Liaison must consult with the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Committee to protect the collegiate-to-Olympic athlete pipeline.

title: Leading the World in Supersonic Flight
agenciesImpacted: Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
aiSummary: This Executive Order launches a federal push to revive commercial supersonic flight over land. It directs the Federal Aviation Administration to lift decades‑old bans, set interim and permanent noise standards, and modernize related rules; instructs the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy to coordinate R&D across multiple agencies; and tasks the Departments of Transportation and State with building international consensus and safety agreements so U.S.‑made supersonic aircraft can operate globally.
deliverable:
Immediate — FAA: Repeal 14 CFR 91.819 & 91.821 to clear legacy regulatory barriers.

180 days — FAA: Repeal 14 CFR 91.817 and issue an interim noise‑based certification standard (modify 91.818).

18 months (~540 days) — FAA: Publish Notice of Proposed Rulemaking for supersonic noise certification under Part 36 and amend 91.817.

24 months (~720 days) — FAA: Issue final rule establishing permanent supersonic noise certification standards.

Ongoing — OSTP (with DoD, DOC, DOT, NASA): Coordinate and share RDT&E data to inform FAA rulemaking and future standards.

Ongoing — DOT/FAA & State: Engage ICAO and negotiate bilateral aviation‑safety agreements enabling international supersonic operations.

title: Keeping Promises to Veterans and Establishing a National Center for Warrior Independence
aiSummary: This Executive Order directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to establish the National Center for Warrior Independence on the West Los Angeles VA campus to serve homeless veterans. The VA is tasked with developing a plan within 120 days to restore capacity to house up to 6,000 veterans by 2028. The order also requires coordination with other federal agencies to redirect applicable funds, expand housing and care access, and promote veteran self-sufficiency. Additional mandates include expanding healthcare options, conducting a feasibility study for a full-service VA medical center in New Hampshire, and improving overall service delivery through interagency cooperation. Accountability measures are also emphasized, with directives to address past personnel decisions and enhance oversight.
deliverable:
VA action plan to restore capacity to house up to 6,000 homeless veterans at the West Los Angeles campus — within 120 days of the order

Report to the President with a plan to reduce Veterans Health Administration appointment wait times (e.g., expanding hours, virtual care) — within 60 days of the order

Feasibility study for expanding the Manchester VA Medical Center — within 30 days of the order

Action plan to expand Manchester VA Medical Center into a full-service facility — within 180 days of the order

Further, the Secretary of the Interior shall take action to ensure that all public monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties within its jurisdiction do not contain descriptions that inappropriately disparages Americans past or living.

title: Designating English as the Official Language of the United States

title: Protecting Second Amendment Rights

title: Establishing a Second Emergency Board to Investigate Disputes Between the Long Island Rail Road Company and Certain of its Employees Represented by Certain Labor Organizations
aiSummary: This EO establishes a second Presidential Emergency Board under § 9A of the Railway Labor Act to investigate and resolve ongoing labor disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and employees represented by five unions. title: Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers
aiSummary: This EO sets a policy that large institutional investors should not buy single-family homes that could otherwise be purchased by families. It directs Treasury to define key terms, requires major housing-related agencies to issue guidance limiting federal facilitation or disposition of homes to such investors (with narrow build-to-rent exceptions), increases antitrust and disclosure scrutiny of investor acquisitions and rental practices, and calls for legislation to codify the policy.

title: Designating Antifa as a Domestic Terrorist Organization

title: Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay

title: Restoring the United States Department of War

title: Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement

title: Adjusting Imports of Automobiles and Automobile Parts into the United States
aiSummary: This proclamation finds that imports of automobiles and certain automobile parts continue to threaten to impair the national security of the United States. All imports of articles specified in Annex I to this proclamation or in any subsequent annex to this proclamation shall be subject to a 25 percent tariff with respect to goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after April 3, 2025, for automobiles, and on the date specified in the Federal Register for automobile parts, but no later than May 3, 2025. For automobiles that qualify for preferential tariff treatment under the USMCA, importers of such automobiles may submit documentation to the Secretary identifying the amount of U.S. content in each model imported into the United States.
deliverable: The Secretary shall establish a process for including additional automobile parts articles within the scope of the tariffs (90 days).

title: Imposing Tariffs on Countries Importing Venezuelan Oil
aiSummary: This EO finds that the actions and policies of the regime of Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela continues to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy of the US. On or after April 2, 2025, a tariff of 25 percent may be imposed on all goods imported into the US from any country that imports Venezuelan oil, whether directly from Venezuela or indirectly through third parties. Duties imposed by this order will be supplemental to duties on imports already imposed pursuant to IEEPA, section 232 of the Trade Expansion of 1962, section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, or any other authority. The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretaries of the Treasury, Commerce, DHS, and the United States Trade Representative, is hereby authorized to determine whether the tariff of 25 percent will be imposed on goods from any country that imports Venezuelan oil, directly or indirectly, on or after April 2, 2025. Once imposed on a country at the Secretary of State’s discretion, the tariff of 25 percent shall expire 1 year after the last date on which the country imported Venezuelan oil, or at an earlier date if the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretaries of State, Treasury, DHS, and the United States Trade Representative, so determines at his/her discretion.
deliverable: The Secretaries of State and Commerce shall submit periodic reports to the President, within 180 days of the date of this order and no less than every 180 days thereafter, assessing the effectiveness of the tariffs described in this order and the ongoing conduct of the Maduro regime (180 days).

title: Amendment to Duties to Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across our Northern Border
aiSummary: This EO adjusts the tariffs imposed on articles of Canada in Executive Order 14193 of February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties to Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border). Specifically, articles that are entered free of duty as a good of Canada under the terms of general note 11 to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), including any treatment set forth in subchapter XXIII of chapter 98 and subchapter XXII of chapter 99 of the HTSUS, as related to the Agreement between the United States of America, United Mexican States, and Canada, shall not be subject to the additional ad valorem rate of duty described in section 2(a) or section 2(b) of Executive Order 14193. Further, the additional rate of duty on potash that is not subject to subsection (a) of this section shall be reduced to 10 percent in lieu of 25 percent. This EO is set to go into effect on March 7, 2025.

title: Addressing the Threat to National Security from Imports of Timber, Lumber
aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of the US to ensure reliable, secure, and resilient domestic supply chains of timber, lumber, and their derivative products. Further, the US must explore whether subsidies and foreign government support for foreign timber, lumber, and their derivative products necessitates action under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act to evaluate the impact on national security. This EO directs the Secretary of Commerce to initiate an investigation under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act to determine the effects on the national security of imports of timber, lumber, and their derivative products. Further, The Secretary of Commerce shall consult with the Secretary of Defense and the heads of other relevant agencies to evaluate the national security risks associated with imports of timber, lumber, and their derivative products and submit a report to the President.
deliverable: The Secretary of Commerce shall consult with the Secretary of Defense and the heads of other relevant  agencies to evaluate the national security risks associated with imports of timber, lumber, and their derivative products and submit a report to the President (270 days).

title: Addressing the Threat to National Security from Imports of Copper
aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of the US to ensure a reliable, secure, and resilient domestic copper supply chain. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to initiate an investigation under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act to determine the effects on national security of imports of copper in all forms and assess it based on 19 U.S.C. 1862(d) factors, and other factors as listed by the EO. The Secretary of Commerce shall consult with Secretaries of Defense, Energy, and Interior to evaluate national security risks associated with copper import dependency.

title: Defending American Companies and Innovators from Overseas Extortion and Unfair Fines and Penalties
aiSummary: This memo states that it is the policy of this administration that when a foreign government imposes a fine, penalty, tax, or other burden that is discriminatory, disproportionate, or designed to transfer significant funds or intellectual property from American companies to the foreign government, this Administration will act, imposing tariffs and taking such other responsive actions necessary to mitigate the harm to the United States. This memo directs the US Trade Representative to determine whether to renew various investigations of DSTs in specific countries. The Secretary of Treasury, Secretary of Commerce, and US Trade Representative shall identify trade and other regulatory practices by other countries that discriminate against or disproportionately affect US global competitiveness in the digital economy OR limit free speech and recommend appropriate actions to counter this.

title: America First Trade Policy
aiSummary: Requires investigations to be conducted by Treasury, Commerce, and the Trade Representative relating to trade deficits in goods, the establishment of a External Revenue Service to collect tariffs and other foreign trade-related revenues, and the impact related to participation in US-Mexico-Canada Agreement. Also requires review of trade agreements and potential changes to these agreements, including potential new agreements on a bilateral or sector-specific basis to obtain export market access for Americans and a review of the agreements between the US and China. Commerce and DoD are tasked with conducting an economic and security review related to imports and exports.
timelineNotes: Reviews and investigations, findings, identifications, and recommendations are due April 1, 2025, with the exception of an OMB report due April 30, 2025.

title: The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Global Tax Deal (Global Tax Deal)
aiSummary: Requires notice to the OECD that the Global Tax Deal has no force in the US. Rescinds any actions or commitments made by the prior administration on behalf of the United States with respect to the Global Tax Deal. Directs the Secretary of the Treasury and US Trade Representative to investigate whether any foreign countries are not in compliance with tax treaties with the US or have any tax rules in place that disproportionately affect American companies.
timelineNotes: No timeline provided for notice to the OECD.
deliverable: Impose a 10% ad valorem duty on all PRC-origin goods — effective May 14, 2025

title: Suspending Duty-Free De Minimus Treatment for all Countries
aiSummary: This EO ends the duty-free de minimis exemption provided under 19 U.S.C. 1321(a)(2)(C) for any shipment of articles not covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b), regardless of value, country of origin, mode of transportation, or method of entry.  Further, all such shipments, except those sent through the international postal network, shall be subject to all applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges. International postal shipments not covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b) shall be subject to the duty rates described in this order.

title: Adjusting Imports of Aluminum into the United States
aiSummary: This proclamation suspends previous proclamations regarding aluminum imports from various countries as of 3/12/2025. Further, a 25% ad valorem rate of duty is implemented for all imports of aluminum into the US beginning 3/12/25 with no exceptions. All aluminum and aluminum derivative articles from Russia or containing Russian aluminum will be subject to a 200% ad valorem rate. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to establish a process for additional steel ad valorem duties within 90 days.
deliverable: The Secretary of Commerce is directed to establish a process for additional aluminum ad valorem duties (90 days).

title: Adjusting Imports of Steel into the United States
aiSummary: This proclamation suspends previous proclamations regarding steel imports from various countries as of 3/12/2025. Further, a 25% ad valorem rate of duty is implemented for all imports of steels and aluminum into the US beginning 3/12/25 with no exceptions. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to establish a process for additional steel ad valorem duties within 90 days.
deliverable: The Secretary of Commerce is directed to establish a process for additional steel ad valorem duties (90 days).

title: Modifying Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
aiSummary: This EO orders the reduction of additional tariffs on certain Chinese goods from 20 percent to 10 percent, effective November 10, 2025, while continuing to monitor China's compliance with these measures. The Secretary of Homeland Security and other officials will oversee implementation, and further action may be taken if China fails to meet its obligations under this agreement.

title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates Consistent with the Economic and Trade Arrangement between the United States and the People's Republic of China
aiSummary: This EO suspends heightened reciprocal tariffs on imports from China until November 10, 2026. This arrangement is intended to help reduce the U.S. trade deficit, strengthen national security and economic interests, and will be monitored for compliance, with the option for further action should China fail to meet its commitments.

title: Modifying the Scope of the Reciprocal Tariff with Respect to Certain Agricultural Products
aiSummary: This EO directs that certain agricultural products be exempted from reciprocal tariffs previously imposed to address national security concerns arising from persistent U.S. goods trade deficits, effective November 13, 2025, with corresponding updates to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule and refund procedures. Relevant officials will continue to monitor the situation and have authority to take further action as necessary, while all departments are directed to implement these changes in accordance with applicable law.

title: Adjusting Imports of Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles , Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicle Parts, and Buses into the United States
aiSummary: This proclamation found that rising imports of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, vehicle parts, and buses threaten U.S. national security by undermining domestic supply chains critical to defense, emergency response, and infrastructure. In response, the President has imposed new tariffs and established offset programs to strengthen domestic manufacturing, safeguard supply chains, and maintain U.S. control over essential vehicle and part production.

title: Modifying the Scope of Tariffs on the Government of Brazil
aiSummary: This EO exempts certain Brazilian agricultural products from previously imposed tariffs due to initial progress in bilateral negotiations, while directing federal agencies to implement and monitor these changes.

title: Regarding the Acquisition of Certain Assets of Emcore Corporation by Hiefo Corporation
aiSummary: This EO finds credible evidence that HieFo Corporation—controlled by a citizen of the People’s Republic of China—may threaten U.S. national security through its completed April 30, 2024 acquisition of EMCORE’s digital chip and related wafer design/fabrication/processing assets, and asserts other laws are insufficient to address the risk. It therefore prohibits the transaction and any ongoing HieFo ownership, requires divestment within 180 days (subject to CFIUS extension), and imposes interim access, transfer, reporting, and audit/verification controls enforced and overseen by CFIUS.

title: Enforcing Commonsense Rules of the Road for America's Truck Drivers
aiSummary: This EO directs enforcement of an English language requirement to operate a commercial motor vehicle. Further, Secretary of Transportation shall review state commercial driver’s licenses to evaluate any irregularities and validate authenticity.
